newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone sets rebels December 1 deadline.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone sets rebels December 1 deadline.

text.p: Sierra Leone's President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah has set rebels a December 1 deadline to lay down their weapons or face military action.
The warning, delivered in the eastern town of Kenema on Sunday, was in spite of a fragile truce that has kept alive hopes of a peace settlement since Kabbah took office in March.
The Revolutionary United Front rebels, who took up arms in 1991, issued a statement on Monday saying that while they still backed a negotiated settlement they would not be intimidated.

"My government will have no alternative but to use the military option against RUF leader Foday Sankoh and his fighters if he fails to order his men to lay down arms as scheduled by the government on December 1," Tejan Kabbah said in Kenema at the start of a visit to the West African country's eastern region.
Tejan Kabbah, whose election in March ended four years of army rule, met Sankoh in Ivory Coast in April and extended a truce agreed with the former military government indefinitely.
Since then there have been repeated attacks around the impoverished nation, with each side blaming the other.
The rebels, in a statement released in Ivory Coast where Sankoh has been since before the April talks, accused Kabbah's government of seeking to provoke a military solution.

"There is a serious danger of the skirmishes degenerating into the resumption of full-scale hostilities," it said, accusing the government of using Kamajor traditional hunters as surrogate fighters against the rebels.
Tejan Kabbah on Sunday praised the Kamajors: "I don't see how I can tell you stop...It's your business to protect yourselves."
